slv1_001: Afternoon clinic hours had just wrapped up. Ryuji Sakaguchi pushed open the door to the staff lounge to pour himself a cup of coffee and spotted Shiori Fujisaki sitting alone at a small round table by the window, cradling a freshly steeped cup of hot black tea.
slv1_002: She wasn't flipping through the files beside her—only looking down at the tea bag drifting in her cup, a faint, helpless wry smile lingering around her brow and eyes.
slv1_003: “Good afternoon, Dr. Fujisaki. Clinic finished right on time today?”
slv1_004: At the sound of his voice, she looked up and set her teacup neatly onto its saucer.
slv1_005: “Ah—good afternoon, Dr. Sakaguchi. Today's follow-up patients were all very cooperative. I just saw the last one out and came by to rest for five minutes.”
slv1_006: Ryuji stepped over to the counter to pour a cup of black coffee; turning back, he noticed the trace of amusement that hadn't quite faded from the corners of her eyes.
slv1_007: “Seeing you stare into your teacup like that just now—did something amusing happen?”
slv1_008: She pressed her lips together lightly and brushed the rim of her cup with her fingertips.
slv1_009: “...Did you catch that, Dr. Sakaguchi? It really wasn't anything major. Just now, the last young woman who came in for suture removal and follow-up suddenly pulled the exam room door halfway shut right before leaving.”
slv1_010: “Had a private question she wanted to ask on the way out?”
slv1_011: “I thought she still had concerns about post-op care too, so I was just about to reopen her chart folder when she suddenly pulled her phone out of her bag and asked in a tiny whisper—whether she could take a photo together with me.”
slv1_013: “Yes. She said that when she went home last time and told her younger sister about her attending physician, her sister refused to believe a word of it and insisted she was making things up—so today she wanted to take a picture back as proof.”
slv1_014: “Sounds like an honest enough reason. Though an exam room really isn't the easiest place for photos.”
slv1_015: “Exactly, so I politely explained the hospital's rules and asked for her understanding regarding workplace discipline. She was actually very sweet—she put her phone away and apologized right on the spot... except the very next second, she slipped her outpatient registration card out of her wallet and held it out to me along with an uncapped pen.”
slv1_016: Ryuji's hand paused for half a beat around his coffee mug.
slv1_017: “...She wanted your autograph on her clinic card?”
slv1_018: She gave a small nod, a trace of helpless absurdity in her voice.
slv1_019: “She pointed so earnestly at the blank space on the back of the card and asked whether, if photos weren't allowed, I could at least sign my name as a discharge keepsake. I sat frozen behind the desk for several seconds, completely at a loss as to where to put the pen.”
slv1_020: “You didn't sign it in the end, I take it?”
slv1_021: “Of course I didn't. I could only tell her half-jokingly that if I actually signed my name across the back of her registration card, the reception nurses on the first floor would probably mistake it for some secret referral code they'd never seen before the next time she checked in.”
slv1_022: Ryuji pulled out the chair across the round table and sat down, the corner of his mouth lifting.
slv1_023: “Wise refusal. Otherwise by next week there might be a hospital urban legend circulating through the first-floor lobby that ‘holders of a clinic card personally signed by Dr. Fujisaki get priority add-on slots.’”
slv1_024: She cast Ryuji a gentle sidelong glance and let out a soft sigh over her teacup.
slv1_025: “Dr. Sakaguchi... why are even you teasing me about it? She was holding up that card with such a serious face, and I had to try very hard not to laugh right there in the exam room so I wouldn't embarrass her.”
slv1_026: “Sorry—the mental picture was just too vivid. In a place like a hospital, nine times out of ten when a doctor solemnly signs something for a patient, it's a surgical consent form or a medical certificate. You don't often see someone happily asking for a signature.”
slv1_027: “When you put it that way, that's true. Two weeks ago she was so anxious about scarring that she could barely sleep; seeing her relaxed enough to make a joke like that after today's checkup really is something her attending doctor ought to be glad about.”
slv1_028: A gentle breeze drifted past the lounge window. Ryuji took a sip of black coffee and naturally followed the thread of conversation.
slv1_029: “Looking after a patient well enough that she wants to keep her clinic card as a souvenir shows how reassuring the atmosphere in your exam room usually is.”
slv1_030: Lowering her gaze to the clear amber tea in her cup, she gave a quiet shake of her head.
slv1_031: “Patients who've come back for a few follow-ups do tend to warm up. Though... every now and then, when a first-time patient walks through the door, things go the exact opposite way.”
slv1_033: “Last Wednesday afternoon, for instance, a middle-aged patient with a long-standing condition transferred in from another hospital. When he pushed open the door and saw me sitting behind the desk, he froze in the doorway for two seconds, even took half a step back to double-check the nameplate outside, and then turned dubiously to the nurse to ask—‘Is the person on duty today really the attending physician herself, and not someone hired for promotional photos?’”
slv1_034: “Mistook you for a poster-model doctor hired for publicity shots?”
slv1_035: “More or less. Even after sitting down, he still looked uneasy—he stared at my face for quite a while before tactfully asking whether, since his old scans were rather complicated, we ought to call in a more senior attending from the department to review them together.”
slv1_036: Ryuji didn't rush to express indignation on her behalf; he simply looked at her calmly and asked on.
slv1_037: “When you run into a patient with preconceptions like that, how do you usually handle it?”
slv1_038: Her posture remained poised, her voice steady and gentle without a hint of pique or grievance.
slv1_039: “There's really no need to argue the point. When a patient has been to several hospitals without getting a clear answer, it's completely natural for them to feel anxious. So I invited him to sit down first, sorted the thick stack of old test reports he'd brought into chronological order, and sketched out on paper—point by point—why his previous rounds of medication hadn't worked and which two indicators we needed to rule out next.”
slv1_041: “By around the third minute, he uncrossed the arms he'd been keeping folded across his chest all on his own. Right before leaving, he even asked whether he could book the same slot with me again for next week's follow-up.”
slv1_042: “No surprise there. Laying the chart out and explaining it clearly works better than any speech about credentials.”
slv1_043: Cradling the warm teacup lightly in both hands, she let her gaze rest on the pale wood grain of the tabletop, her voice softening just a little.
slv1_044: “Yes—during consultations themselves, little things like that don't affect my judgment. It's only once in a while, after I close the clinic log and the room falls quiet, that it leaves a slightly odd feeling.”
slv1_046: “How should I put it... We all wear the exact same white coat and do the exact same work a physician is meant to do every day, yet before I even pick up my stethoscope or begin analyzing the case, what people notice first always seems to be everything outside of that.”
slv1_047: “Whether someone finds it a novelty and asks for my autograph, or walks in doubting whether I'm qualified to treat them—when you think about it, either way they see the ‘appearance’ at first glance, and only afterward does it get around to the ‘doctor.’”
slv1_048: Ryuji listened quietly until she finished. Offering neither an easy compliment about her looks nor a grand speech of reassurance, he spoke in the same matter-of-fact tone he might use on daily rounds.
slv1_049: “Other doctors get to go straight to the chart the moment someone walks in, whereas you have to spend three extra minutes bringing their attention back to the condition itself—having an extra step tacked onto your workflow for no reason would leave anyone feeling a little exasperated.”
slv1_050: She didn't seem to expect Ryuji to respond from that angle. She blinked once, and the faint trace of helplessness in her eyes melted away as her brows curved into a genuine, unguarded smile.
slv1_051: “...‘An extra step in the workflow,’ huh? Put like that, Dr. Sakaguchi, it really does sound like just another routine part of history-taking—much less something to dwell on.”
slv1_052: In lighter spirits, Shiori Fujisaki lifted her cup for a sip of tea, then drew an issue of a recent medical journal lying open near the edge of the table closer to slip a bookmark inside.
slv1_053: Ryuji Sakaguchi's gaze naturally brushed across the open spread, where a frontier research paper on cellular repair mechanisms was printed alongside several remarkably bold experimental model diagrams.
slv1_054: “Reading the latest special issue on medical research?”
slv1_055: She glanced down at the page, her fingertips resting lightly beside the author byline.
slv1_056: “Yes—the new issue arrived at the reading corner this morning, so I leafed through a few pages during my break. The first author of this paper happens to be an old classmate of mine from school.”
slv1_057: Following the tip of her finger, Ryuji glanced at the kanji printed on the byline.
slv1_058: “‘Yuina Himoo’... That's an uncommon surname. Publishing research of this weight as first author in a core journal at our age is seriously impressive.”
slv1_059: At the mention of that name, her expression relaxed naturally into sincere admiration.
slv1_060: “Yuina has been like that ever since our student days. No matter how obscure or thorny a research topic was, once it landed in her hands she could always find an angle nobody else would ever have imagined.”
slv1_062: “Yes. Purely in terms of original medical research, I truly don't match up to her.”
slv1_063: “You say that without a second's hesitation.”
slv1_064: There wasn't a trace of reluctance or insecurity on her face—her candor sounded almost buoyant.
slv1_065: “Because I genuinely admire her. When it comes to making clinical judgments within established medicine and putting together sound, reliable treatment plans for patients, I'm confident I won't lose to anyone; when it comes to overturning settled assumptions and breaking open unknown territory, though, Yuina was born to stand on the very frontier.”
slv1_067: “When ordinary people see experimental data that doesn't match the textbook, their first instinct is usually to check which step of the protocol they messed up. When Yuina spots anomalous data, her eyes light up on the spot—her first instinct is to suspect that mainstream theory itself left something out.”
slv1_068: Recalling how her old friend used to be, a fond, amused warmth surfaced in Shiori Fujisaki's eyes.
slv1_069: “The moment she catches the scent of a new hypothesis, she can bury herself in stacks of literature and lab benches for days on end, completely deaf to anyone telling her to rest. When it comes to research, nobody is bolder or more confident than she is.”
slv1_070: “Questioning mainstream theory head-on definitely takes nerve. Was it like that back when the two of you ran lab work together?”
slv1_071: She gently closed the journal and rested her fingers on its cover, as though picturing their student laboratory days.
slv1_072: “It really was. Outside of work we got along wonderfully, yet the instant the direction of an experiment came up, neither of us could ever talk the other around. Once, when we were paired on a project, our samples yielded a set of anomalous readings far outside expectations—the moment Yuina read the log, she wanted to expand the experimental conditions right then and there to chase down the underlying reaction mechanism.”
slv1_073: “And you argued for pausing to verify first?”
slv1_074: “Yes. I insisted on completing normal-tissue controls and replicate validation first—making sure the readings were genuinely reproducible and mapping out any potential tissue-damage risks before pushing further. She stood across the lab bench holding her clipboard, refusing to yield half a step, and asked me right back—‘If we pour all our energy into playing it safe the moment we brush against a new mechanism, what happens if the real breakthrough slips past while we're hesitating?’”
slv1_075: “We debated it all the way to the end without either of us giving ground easily... Even today, flipping through her paper and seeing designs that press decisively deeper the instant an anomaly appears, half of me admires her sharpness while the other half still instinctively flips ahead to check her control data and risk boundaries first.”
slv1_076: “Checking validation and risk boundaries first sounds very much like Dr. Fujisaki.”
slv1_077: Glancing at the cover of the journal, Ryuji added an offhand remark.
slv1_078: “Still, having a research prodigy like that for an old classmate—if we ever run into a refractory case here at Hoshimi where conventional protocols hit a wall, there might really come a day when we ask Dr. Himoo for her insight.”
slv1_079: “If a day ever comes when we need to call on Yuina, the case itself will surely be a daunting one... Though knowing her, she really might come up with an approach nobody else could envision—even if the two of us would inevitably end up arguing a few rounds again.”
slv1_080: Down the distant corridor came the faint footsteps of the afternoon ward handover as the minute hand of the lounge wall clock clicked softly onto three-thirty.
slv1_081: Glancing at her wristwatch, she rose neatly to her feet at once.
slv1_082: “Ah... it's three-thirty already before I knew it. I'm truly sorry, Dr. Sakaguchi—you finally came to the lounge for a quiet moment, and ended up listening to me ramble all by myself about clinic trivia and an old classmate.”
slv1_083: Ryuji Sakaguchi stood up as well, carrying his empty coffee mug over to the sink with an easy, unhurried air.
slv1_084: “No need to apologize. Those fifteen minutes beat staring at the duty roster over plain coffee by a mile. Besides, hearing Dr. Fujisaki talk about life outside the exam room for once was pretty refreshing.”
slv1_085: Picking up her own teacup to rinse it at the counter, she tilted her head slightly to look at Ryuji.
slv1_086: “Refreshing... Does that mean I normally come across as rather dull around the hospital?”
slv1_087: “Only that you handle everything around the hospital so impeccably I figured you might not be someone to joke around with lightly—I didn't expect a patient asking for an autograph on a clinic card to stump you too.”
slv1_088: Her hands paused for half a second as she dried her fingers, and then she let out a soft laugh—no longer the textbook-polite courtesy of the consulting room, even the line of her shoulders easing naturally.
slv1_089: “...So in Dr. Sakaguchi's eyes, I usually seem that unapproachable. Still, please do keep that clinic-card story strictly between us—if word of it ever reached emergency or surgery, everyone would probably tease me about it for weeks.”
slv1_091: She slid the medical journal neatly back into its place on the reading-corner shelf, then turned and gave Ryuji Sakaguchi a gentle nod.
slv1_092: “Thank you for listening to me talk today, Dr. Sakaguchi. I'll head back to the ward to check on this afternoon's follow-up labs—best of luck with the rest of your shift.”
slv1_094: With a composed, gentle expression, Shiori Fujisaki pushed open the door and stepped out into the corridor. A faint trace of black tea lingered in the quiet lounge, the polite distance between two ordinary colleagues having quietly narrowed by half a step before either of them realized it.
